title: Alnwick Dolphins
text:
Welcome to Alnwick Dolphins!
This manual is intended to arm you with all the information you need to confidently embark on your Dolphins career, or to support your swimmer to reach their goals.
For more from Alnwick Dolphins, you can check out our website.
Key information is also shown on the noticeboards in the spectator area at Willowburn Sports and Leisure Centre Pool.
You can also follow us on Facebook and X.

title: 1  How to join Alnwick Dolphins
text:
1.1 How fit/capable do I need to be to try out?
All swimmers enter the club by first having a short Swimming Taster Session. Times and dates for these are advertised on our website and on the notice boards at poolside. If you wish to take part in a taster session, please register your interest for the next available session.
To flourish at Alnwick Dolphins, new swimmers need to be confident in the water, typically having completed the equivalent of Stage 6 of the Swim England Swimming Development Programme, and being at least 7 years old.
crumbs: 1  How to join Alnwick Dolphins

title: 1  How to join Alnwick Dolphins
section: 1.2 What happens at a taster session?
text:
1.2 What happens at a taster session?
Please arrive at your session promptly so the group can start together. No extra kit is needed, just your usual swimming costume and goggles. You will be welcomed by the coach and the session will be explained to you.
You will be asked to show the coach several swim strokes, but you don’t need to be fast, or be able to swim a very long way. We are looking for potential, not the finished product! The coaches will be appraising the swimmer for their physical abilities as well as how they cope with the instructions given.
After the Taster Session, the coaches will convene to discuss each swimmers performance and determine who they feel is ready to join the club. You will be notified by email the result of the Taster Session within 2 weeks. But don’t worry if you don’t make it this time, you can always try again at a future Taster Session!
crumbs: 1  How to join Alnwick Dolphins

title: 1  How to join Alnwick Dolphins
text:
1.3 🚀 I got in!! Now what?
To become a member of the club, you will be asked to

read and sign a swimmers code of conduct
read and sign a parent/carers code of conduct
register with Swim England as a Club Compete member (currently £37.35 annually, this enables you to compete at licensed events, provides insurance and other member benefits)
sign up to use Swim Manager, adding your bank details to enable payments to be taken monthly.

Once signed up, check your training timetable (which you can find on Swim Manager), ensure you have the kit you need, then get started on your Alnwick Dolphins journey! 🐬
Have a look at the training page to see what goes on at a typical training session.

title: 2  Swim Manager
text:
SwimManager Logo


Most UK amateur swimming clubs use Swim Manager, which is a software platform for managing their club. You will be given an account on Swim Manager when you join the club. This is our central information repository for everything we do. You can access your account via the mobile app (available on Apple and Android devices) or through a browser.
The main roles Swim Manager plays are:

storing information about members; name, age, squad, PB times
training schedules
managing galas; entries, information, payments, volunteer sign-up
collecting club fees
buying Alnwick Dolphins branded kit
communications with members
storing club certifications and policies

If you are having any difficulties with your SwimManager account, please contact the Club Secretary.

title: 3  Training
text:
3.1 What happens at a training session?
Swimmers arrive ready to swim 10 mins before the session is scheduled to start so they can take part in poolside warm ups. There is no need to sign in at reception when you arrive, simply head into the changing rooms and get ready, grab your goggles (and swim cap if you have one), have a quick shower then make your way to the pool area where your coaches should be waiting.
Supporters are free to watch the session if they wish from the seating area, but please do not interfere with the coaches instructions.
Swimmers in higher squads will bring extra kit with them to the poolside, but don’t worry, you don’t need everything on day 1!

title: 3  Training
text:
Important



Please note that:

only swimmers and staff are allowed poolside
you may not pass through the reception area unless fully clothed

title: 3  Training
text:
3.2 What kit do I need?
For all swimmers, you need a well fitting swimming costume and goggles, a swim cap and water bottle. Once you’ve joined the club you will be provided a Dolphins swimming cap and water bottle, but it may take a few weeks to arrive, so feel free to bring your own until then.
Extra kit is needed as you progress through the squads:
From Great White Sharks onwards:

kickboard
fins (flippers)
pull buoy

Tiger Sharks and above:

snorkel
hand paddles







Important



For competitions, you also need to have an Alnwick Dolphins team swim cap, and an Alnwick Dolphins Team T-shirt. These can be purchased through Swim Manager.

title: 3  Training
text:
3.3 Lane etiquette
The following behavioural rules are designed to ensure everyone leaves a training session feeling positive and respected.

arrive on time and ready to swim
don’t get out of the pool during sets
don’t swim too close to the person in front: If you need to overtake, touch their toes gently but firmly, then at the end of the lane they will allow you to push off first.
allow overtaking at lane ends only, if your toes are touched
no booing of other swimmers, whether in our team or others
pay attention to your coach at all times

title: 4  Squads
text:
Squads are groups of swimmers at a similar stage of development, who train together throughout the week. As swimmers progress through the squads from Flying Fish right up to Performance level, the focus of their training changes, as does the timing and frequency of training sessions (and consequently the training fees also).
Progression up a squad is at the discretion of the coaches, and every swimmer progresses at their own rate. Every training session, the coaches are continually assessing the swimmers abilities and ambition, and when they feel they are ready for more, they may offer them a place in the next squad up, occasionally after having them spend a few trial training sessions in with the higher group to see how they cope.
The squads, the number of hours a week they train and the number of swimming sessions per week is shown below. Swimmers are expected to be present for all of their sessions every week, except in exceptional circumstances. title: 5  Land Training 🏋️
text:
5.1 Why do we train on land?
For Marlins and above, swimmers are encouraged to join in with one hour a week of expert-led ‘land training’ (i.e. gym work).
We are very lucky that, through member contacts, Dolphins are able to undertake a targeted group training session for an hour weekly at Real Fitness in Alnwick.
These sessions cost just £2.50 each, and have limited spaces. You can sign up via their website.
To book a session, select the Saturday 10:15 ‘Dolphins S and C Training’ entry in their diary on the landing page and follow instructions to book a slot.
Collette (a.k.a Colls) of Real Fitness says:
The gym lets us do things the pool simply cannot. We can add resistance, build strength and develop power in ways that are not possible in water, where the body is supported and the resistance changes with how fast they move. It also means their bones get loading they would not otherwise get, which matters during the teenage years when a large proportion of adult bone is laid down. None of this replaces swimming. It complements it, and the two together tend to produce better swimmers than swimming alone.
Starts and turns are the moments in a race where the feet are pressed against something solid, and that is where leg strength really shows. In a sprint, the start can account for a good chunk of the race, and the turns even more in a short course pool. Strength and power measured on land line up closely with how well swimmers do both. The evidence generally points the same way: swimmers who train in the pool and on land tend to progress better than those who only swim.
There is also the question of control. However strong a swimmer is, that strength only reaches the water if they can hold themselves steady through the trunk, ribs, shoulders and hips. A good deal of what we do is building that.
A note on safety:
Strength training for young people is well supported when it is properly supervised and sensibly prescribed. It does not affect growth or growth plates, and injury rates are lower than in most field sports. We do want to challenge them, because that is where the benefit comes from, but I always take a view on how they arrive and adjust the session accordingly.

title: 6  Safeguarding
text:
The safety of our swimmers is out utmost priority. We are a SwimMark Accredited Club, which means that we have Swim England’s highest standards of safe and effective practice in place. The Club Affiliation process exists so new and existing members know the club is well run and our personnel have the necessary safeguarding checks and appropriate qualifications in place to ensure members’ safety.
We have a nominated SwimMark Coordinator, a Welfare Officer, and safeguarding training requirements for all key roles. Please see our Club Constitution for more details.

title: 7  Competitions (galas)
text:
7.1 What happens at a gala?
All swimmers are encouraged to take part in stage-appropriate galas as they are fun, exciting, motivating and excellent for development.
Our annual competition calendar tends to include four home galas (which all swimmers are expected to enter where possible) and several away galas in the North East Region. You are not expected to enter every gala, and you can discuss which ones would suit your swimmer with their coach at any time.
The competition season runs from about August to June.
For every gala, be it home or away, a (DBS checked) Team Manager (often more than one) is required to look after the swimmers, organise itineraries and generally help with the smooth running of the event. Where team transport is available for attending away galas, new swimmers can be confident that the Team Managers are there to look out for them, and their whole team will make sure they have a positive, fun experience.
Swimmers make their way to the venue ready to start the group warm up at the scheduled time. They will have a team area on poolside where they will rest between races, eat and drink something, play games (no electronic devices allowed) or read books. Team Managers and Marshalls will ensure each swimmer is ready to compete when their events come around. There is often access to a ‘cool down pool’ provided during the event so that athletes can keep their muscles warm between races and cool down after intense swimming.
Typical kit needed for a gala includes:

title: 7  Competitions (galas)
text:
swimming costume
goggles (plus a spare pair)
towels (one for poolside, one for after)
team swim cap
team T-shirt
enough healthy food and water for the duration of the event
something to occupy them poolside between races (e.g. book, card games etc.)

title: 7  Competitions (galas)
text:
7.2 Gala levels
Galas range from ‘just for fun’ unlicensed events, right up to professional National extravaganzas. You can tell how ‘serious’ a gala is by its ‘level’, which dictates how official is it, what its results times can be used for and who can enter. Level 4 galas require a license, but are the entry-level events. Level 3 galas require specific qualified officials to be present, and results can be used for entry to level 2 galas. At Alnwick, the galas we host are all level 3 or 4.

7.2.1 Home galas
The club typically hosts the following galas at the following times of the year. For all except the Club Championships, other clubs in the region are invited to participate.

Autumn Invitational (October)
Distance Time Trial (Level 4, November, for County and Performance Squads)
New Year Invitational (January)
Club Championships (June)



7.2.2 Away galas
Each year the Competition Secretary along with the Committee will identify externally hosted galas that fit in with the club’s existing commitments, and make them available to enter via Swim Manager.
The coaches will decide which squads should target which galas, to enable them to obtain the relevant qualifying times for future events and provide a range of different experiences for the squads.
Typically, the galas where entry is encouraged for all junior swimmers include:

7.2.2.1 Newcastle Swim Team’s Shrip Galas
Held at Tynemouth pool at vaious times throughout the season, these fun events are a great introduction to competitions for younger (8-12 years) swimmers. These are level 4 galas.


7.2.2.2 Mini Morpeth Meet
A super fun, super friendly introduction to racing, this unlicensed event usually occurs in early Winter.


7.2.2.3 South Tyneside Meets
A level 3 gala held in South Shields for swimmers 9+. Often run in Spring and Autumn.


7.2.2.4 Durham Medley Challenge
The Durham Medley Challenge (Level 3) is a little different to the usual galas. For the flat fee of £25 per swimmer, each swimmer is entered into either 50m or 100m events in each stoke depending on their age on the day.


7.2.2.5 Juniour (‘Diddy’) League
Teams from all over the North East compete for the title of Junior League Champions. The competition is fun, exciting, very competitive and very, very loud with a mixture of individual and team relay events. The league consists of 3 divisions and teams are promoted and relegated between the divisions depending on where they finish. Typically there are two or three ‘heats’ before the Junior League Finals, held in September. These galas are usually NOT added to Swim Manager but are organised separately.

Other galas require swimmers to have achieved qualifying times to enter, and may change from year to year. You can find out more about each upcoming competition on our competition calendar which is emailed out to all parents at the start of the new season.
If you have questions about any of the above, please contact the competition secretary.
